alternate_names: Takht Sri Darbar Sahib Damdama Sahib

history.summary: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA (ONE OF THE FIVE TAKHTS), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. CSV town 'Bathinda' corrected to Talwandi Sabo, about 28 km southeast of Bathinda, where the shrine stands. Guru Gobind Singh stayed here in 1705 after the battles of Anandpur Sahib, Chamkaur Sahib and Muktsar, and prepared the final recension of the Guru Granth Sahib here (the Damdama Sahib Bir, transcribed by Bhai Mani Singh). 'Damdama' means resting place; the Guru also blessed the town as a centre of learning, hence 'Guru Ki Kashi'. It is the headquarters of the Nihang (armed Sikh) order. Guru Tegh Bahadur is said to have visited earlier. The complex includes the underground Bhora Sahib meditation chamber, relics of Guru Gobind Singh (sword, matchlock, mirror, pothi), and three sarovars: Nanksar, Akalsar and Gurusar. One account says the first structure was raised by Sardar Bhagel Singh in 1783 and later renovated by Maharaja Ranjit Singh (source-reported, verify). It was the last and most recent of the five Takhts to be formally recognised, by SGPC decision in November 1966.

name: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib
town_description: Talwandi Sabo is a historic town in Bathinda district of Punjab, about 28 km southeast of Bathinda city. Known to Sikhs as 'Guru Ki Kashi' (the Kashi of the Guru), it is a major seat of Sikh learning and one of the five Takhts. The town is set in the Malwa plains and draws large numbers of pilgrims, especially at Baisakhi.

travel.airport: Nearest domestic airport is Bathinda Airport (~45-50 km) (verify); Chandigarh International Airport ~230 km.
travel.railway: Talwandi Sabo railway station on the Bathinda–Delhi line (~1-2 km from the shrine); major junction at Bathinda (~28-30 km).
travel.road: Well connected by road from Bathinda (28 km) and nearby Malwa towns; local buses and taxis available.

visitor_information.best_time: October to April, when the weather is pleasant; Baisakhi (mid-April) draws the largest gatherings.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily, typically early morning to late evening; langar served. Exact daily timings not confirmed (verify).
